P1.reason: A's groups are cleaner: setup, win/loss, forward movement and sideways capture are distinct. B mixes setup with board update and spreads capture over three groups.

differences.reason: Helps: the starting position is its own clear setup rule.
Helps: arrival, stalemate-loss, terminal and goals form one coherent game-end rule.
Helps: forward direction with straight and diagonal moves reads as pawn movement.
Mostly helps: adjacency plus capture is the capture rule, though diagonal also needs beside.
Hurts: mixes the board-update and frame rule with the initial position, two unrelated ideas.
Hurts: capture definition tacked onto the game-end rule muddles it.
Mixed: complete movement rule including capture and empty, but overlaps heavily with B4.
Hurts: adjacency with diagonal and capture duplicates B3, giving redundant, overlapping groups.
